Path: studio — the design canvas shows and edits what the author wrote, in every language | 缺项 (`AppNavCanvas`'s `navLabel` reads a nav label only as a string and shows "Item N" for a locale map; `renameItem` writes a plain string, replacing the whole map) | P2

## Triage: first grade — `bug` · `priority:p2` · `domain:ui` · `area:studio` · `pm:queue`. Direction (triage's call): resolve for display, and rename **only the current locale's entry** of a map

Triage: lands in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/AppNavCanvas.tsx` ⇒ `domain:ui`. It is objectui#11100's family (closed by PR objectui#11127 for the preview).

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-09-29T18:53Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

**Why p2, not p3 like objectui#11100.** Display alone would be p3. But the rename path, read and not measured, replaces an author's per-locale map with a plain string, which silently deletes every other language's text. That is a loss of authored metadata.

**Direction.**
- **Display:** `navLabel` resolves through the spec's `resolveI18nLabel(label, locale)` in the designer locale, as `AppPreview` now does. "Item N" stays only for a label that is truly absent.
- **Rename:** on a map-labelled item, an inline rename writes **the designer locale's entry** and keeps every other entry. On a plain-string label it writes the string, as today. ⛔ Never replace a map with a string.
  - This is the mainstream rule: editing a translated label edits that language.
  - The one exception: a map with no entry for the designer locale gains one.
- **Pins:**
  - A map-labelled item shows the resolved text under en and zh in design mode.
  - Renaming it under zh changes only `zh-CN`, and `en` survives.
  - A plain-string item renames as today (the control).
- **Coordinate:** objectui#10862 (`pm:queue`) moves this family's chrome strings. The files overlap, so whichever lands second rebases.

## Carrier note: `navLabel`'s absent-label fallback `Item N` also reads a designer catalogue row · `domain:ui` seat 2 · 2026-09-29T19:26Z

`session_011p7ikEivgXefNDaE5S5Uec`, at the ACCEPT of PR objectui#11134 (objectui#10862 slice 4, the family's last slice).

**The finding.** `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/AppNavCanvas.tsx:168` renders `` `Item ${i + 1}` `` for a nav item with no label. That is English under zh-CN. The source is objectui#10862's closure census: its dev's AST pass over `previews/` and `external/`, and that PR's contract review (`5897115110`, ③).

**Why it is on this card.** objectui#10862's dispatch barred this file's label logic, because this card rewrites `navLabel`. The seat ruled the fallback this card's (the review judged that right). With this carrier, objectui#10862 closes.

**What it asks of this card.** Your direction keeps "Item N" for a truly absent label. That fallback reads a designer catalogue row with the index as a hole, for example a new `engine.appNav.item` = `Item {{n}}`, en byte-equal, with zh added. It reads that row through the designer `t` in the same locale `navLabel` now resolves in. Pin: a zh render of an unlabelled item. This adds one row and one line to the edit this card already makes, and moves no other file.
